Back The CCJE holds its 27th plenary meeting and adopts a new Opinion on the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in the judicial process

The 27th plenary meeting of the CCJE was held on 23-25 November 2026 in Strasbourg. The CCJE adopted Opinion No. 29 (2026) on the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in the judicial process. This important topic was considered through the prism of relevant instruments of the Council of Europe, in particular the Framework Convention on artificial intelligence and human rights, democracy and the rule of law of 2024, and the tools of the European Commission for the Efficiency of Justice (CEPEJ).

The adopted Opinion recognises that the use of AI in the judicial process can be beneficial for improving the access to justice and promoting the rule of law, and its safe and appropriate use should be welcomed. Such use should be consistent with fundamental constitutional and human rights, particularly the rights guaranteed by the European Convention on Human Rights, and should ensure that judicial decision making remains the judge’s sole responsibility.

The CCJE adopted also a thematic study on courts and environmental litigation, addressing challenges in dealing with environmental cases from the perspective of courts. Finally, in response to a request of the Committee of Ministers of the Council of Europe, it also adopted Comments on Recommendation 2314 (2026) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe addressing the possibility of sanctions in respect of the judges of the International Criminal Court (ICC).
